Tools for Analyzing the Survey of Consumer Finances (SCF)

Source: R/scf-package.R
scf.Rd

The scf package streamlines analysis of the U.S. Federal Reserve’s Survey of Consumer Finances — a nationally representative, multiply-imputed survey of U.S. household finances.

Details

This package helps applied researchers, economists, and social scientists work with the SCF’s complex design and multiple imputation structure using intuitive, consistent tools.

Key Features

  • Data ingestion: scf_download() and scf_load() to retrieve and prepare SCF data

  • Data transformation: scf_update(), scf_subset() for safe manipulation across implicates

  • Descriptive analysis: scf_mean(), scf_median(), scf_percentile(), scf_corr(), scf_xtab()

  • Regression models: scf_ols(), scf_logit(), scf_glm() with Rubin’s Rules applied automatically

  • Visualization: ggplot2-based plotting functions like scf_plot_dbar()

SCF Overview

The SCF is a triennial household survey conducted by the Federal Reserve Board since 1983. It uses multiple imputation to account for item nonresponse and oversamples wealthy households via a dual-frame sample design.

Each case appears in five implicates, and variance estimation relies on 999 replicate weights. The scf package abstracts this complexity using survey and mitools under the hood.

Learning More

  • Vignette: vignette("SCF-guide") for a step-by-step workflow

  • Federal Reserve SCF site: https://www.federalreserve.gov/econres/scfindex.htm

  • Reference: Kennickell, A. (1998). Multiple Imputation in the Survey of Consumer Finances
